summary: Intermittent DoT resolver truncation returns stale CNAME -> leads to obsolete presigned URL and 416 on shard range fetch
description:
Issue summary: NimbusHealth reports intermittent 416 Range Not Satisfiable and partial shard corruption when Dedicated serving nodes perform parallel shard downloads during nightly rolling updates.

Impact: Several production model endpoints for the customer become degraded for short windows (10-30s) causing retries, extra token spend, and occasional application-level errors for end-users.

Environment: Private deployment (VPC peered to Redwood control plane) in us-east-1. Model shards are stored on presigned S3 URLs (us-east) fetched by serving nodes via VPCE and corporate DNS forwarder which uses DNS-over-TLS (DoT) to upstream resolver.

Observed: Control-plane logs show DNS resolution of the presigned host resolving to an older CNAME occasionally (points to an archived bucket/object snapshot). The presigned URL generated by control-plane is valid but points to an object with a different byte-length than serving nodes expect. When the node issues ranged GETs in parallel, S3 responds 416 (Range Not Satisfiable) or returns a different content-length causing a range-to-byte-offset mismatch and partial shard corruption.

Initial hypothesis: The customer's DoT resolver intermittently responds with a truncated/truncated-EDNS0 UDP reply (TC bit set) which is ignored by the forwarder; fallback to TCP is inconsistent, causing occasional return of stale/A record due to resolver cache sharding. This leads to control-plane selecting the stale host and generating a presigned URL for a different artifact version.
steps_to_reproduce:
1) Deploy a dedicated serving group in customer VPC pegged to us-east.
2) Trigger a model rollout that causes serving nodes to download 32 parallel shard ranges per node.
3) On the customer DNS forwarder, enable verbose DNS-over-TLS logging and watch for UDP truncation/TC flags.
4) Correlate timestamps of any truncated DoT responses with control-plane DNS cache entries and the presigned URL hostnames returned.
5) Reproduce by forcing the forwarder to drop TCP fallback to observe increased rate of 416 responses.
observed_behavior: Occasional 416 responses from S3 during parallel ranged GETs; serving node logs show Content-Length mismatch and 'shard validation failed: expected 10485760 got 524288'. Control-plane DNS cache showed a different CNAME for the presigned host for a ~20s window around the failures. Customer DoT logs show 'truncated response' events at the same timestamps.
expected_behavior: Presigned URLs generated by control-plane resolve consistently to the correct S3 host/object. DoT resolver should gracefully fallback to TCP on EDNS0/UDP truncation and not serve stale cached CNAME/A records. Parallel ranged GETs should succeed without 416s or content-length mismatch.
logs:
[serving-node-1] 2026-03-12T02:14:22Z shard_fetch range=bytes=0-524287 status=416 content-length=524288 expected=10485760
[control-plane] 2026-03-12T02:14:22Z dns-resolve presigned.host -> cname=old-artifact-2026-02-05.s3.amazonaws.com
[dns-forwarder] 2026-03-12T02:14:21Z dot-upstream tcp-fallback=false response=TRUNCATED tc=1
[dns-forwarder] 2026-03-12T02:14:23Z dot-upstream tcp-fallback=true response=OK cname=new-artifact-2026-03-12.s3.amazonaws.com
investigation:
- Support reproduced the issue in a controlled staging repro by toggling TCP fallback on the customer's forwarder; when TCP fallback disabled we saw >90% repro rate.
- Packet captures show EDNS0 UDP responses with TC set from the DoT upstream resolver. Forwarder version 1.4.2 ignored TC flag and did not retry over TCP in ~30% of cases due to a bug in DoT implementation.
- Control-plane caches DNS answers for 30s; when the forwarder returned a stale CNAME on the first UDP response, control-plane cached the stale entry briefly and generated presigned URLs pointing to wrong object versions.
- Correlated timestamps with customer's nightly batch causing heavy DNS parallelism which increased probability of UDP truncation at upstream resolver.
- SRE confirmed S3 objects exist and are intact; the mismatch is purely due to URL pointing at wrong object version.
comments: 2026-03-12 - Aisha Patel (Support): Received initial report from NimbusHealth CS; customer reports intermittent app errors during nightly batch. Collected serving logs and DNS forwarder captures. Assigned to Marco (SRE).

2026-03-12 - Marco Reyes (SRE): Reproduced in staging by disabling TCP fallback on test forwarder. Evidence points to forwarder DoT implementation ignoring TC in some UDP responses. Asking customer for forwarder version and config.
2026-03-12 - NimbusHealth (Customer): We're running vendor DNS forwarder v1.4.2 with custom caching. We'll open a ticket with vendor but need a short-term workaround.

2026-03-13 - Marco Reyes (SRE): Temporary control-plane mitigation deployed: shorten DNS cache TTL for presigned hostnames to 5s for this customer and add content-length validation at presign time (if content-length mismatch on first fetch, re-generate URL). Monitoring for reductions in 416s.

2026-03-14 - Aisha Patel (Support): Customer confirmed errors dropped to near-zero after mitigation. Vendor returned patch v1.4.3 with TCP-fallback fix and EDNS0 handling. Planning full patch rollout on customer's forwarder next maintenance window.
resolution: Partial mitigation applied 2026-03-13: control-plane cache TTL reduced for presigned artifact hostnames for affected customer and presign flow updated to detect immediate content-length mismatches and re-issue presigned URLs once. Customer's vendor released DNS forwarder patch v1.4.3 that ensures TCP fallback on DoT UDP truncation. Full remediation requires customer to apply vendor patch and schedule forwarder restart.
workaround:
1) Apply vendor patch v1.4.3 to DNS forwarder to ensure TCP fallback on DoT truncation.
2) If patch cannot be applied immediately: throttle parallel shard fetches to 4 concurrent ranged GETs per node and add a short jitter between presigned URL generation and first fetch.
3) Temporary control-plane TTL reduction already applied for affected customer.
postmortem_followup:
- Engineering to add automatic detection: if presigned artifact fetch returns 416 or content-length mismatch, control-plane should automatically re-resolve and re-issue presigned URL and surface a diagnostic.
- Documentation: add recommended DoT configuration and a KB article for customers running DoT forwarders.
- Ops: add an alert for surges in DNS 'truncated' events from customer forwarders.
